Why some towers do nothing to some enemies
An enemy's armor is subtracted from every hit it takes. If the hit is 10 and the armor is 3, 7 gets through. At least 1 always gets through, no matter how much armor it has.

Towers that hit many times for little damage (Machine Gun, Multi, Burst) lose a lot against armored enemies. Big-hit towers (Cannon, Sniper) barely notice it. When you hit, a number with the real damage floats up; if it looks gray, the armor ate half or more of the hit: that tower is a bad choice against that enemy.
Burn damage is not reduced by armor, so the Incendiary is just the thing against armored enemies.

Enemies come out of the entrances and follow the path to the exit. Your job is to stop them with towers before they get there. Every enemy that reaches the exit takes lives from you; if you run out of lives, you lose. If you survive all the waves with at least one life, you win the level.
With gold you build and upgrade towers. You start with the level's gold, earn more by killing enemies and get a bonus when each wave ends. You can build at any time, even while a wave is running.

Nothing starts until you press "Start wave": build calmly before that. Between waves there is a countdown; if you don't want to wait, start the next one yourself. Each wave brings enemies with more health than the last, so you have to keep reinforcing your defenses.
Put towers on the bends: enemies spend more time inside the range there. Mix tower types, because every enemy has a weakness (see each enemy's entry under Enemies and each tower's under Towers).

Choose a tower in the bar below (or with the 1 to 8 keys) and click a free grass tile. You'll see the range circle and, in green, that you can build there; in red, that you can't. Right click or Esc cancel.
Every tower has 3 levels. Clicking a built tower opens its panel: there you see its level, its numbers and the Upgrade button (U key). Upgrading costs gold, and at level 3 there is nothing more.

Selling (S key) removes the tower and gives you back part of all the gold you put into it, construction and upgrades included. It's useful for rearranging your defenses when you think of something better.

Every tower chooses whom to shoot: First (the one closest to the exit, the normal one), Last, Strongest (the one with the most health) or Closest (the one nearest to the tower). You change it from the tower's panel. Against a dangerous enemy or a boss, "Strongest" is best; to let nobody through, "First".
What towers do besides dealing damage

Frost slows enemies down: a slowed enemy moves more slowly and looks tinted blue. Several slows don't add up: the strongest one counts, and every new hit restarts the timer. That gives the other towers more time to hit it.
The Incendiary sets things on fire: the enemy takes damage every half second for a few seconds. Fire ignores armor and, while it lasts, the enemy can't heal. Burns don't add up either.
The Cannon damages every enemy near the point of impact: it shines against groups. It doesn't touch flyers.

The Multi shoots several enemies at once. The Burst fires spikes in a circle, and does best on a bend. The Electric fires a bolt that jumps from one enemy to another. The numbers for each level are in each tower's entry.

Some towers hit harder against an enemy that is already slowed by Frost or burning from the Incendiary: the Cannon, the Sniper and the Mortar take advantage of ice, and the Electric of fire. It doesn't matter where the towers are: what matters is that the enemy arrives slowed or burning.

A combo hit shows its number bigger and with a "!": light blue if it came from ice and orange if it came from fire, and a "ting" sounds. While an enemy is ready for a combo, a small target of that color shows next to its health bar. How much each combo adds is in each tower's entry.

The Disruptor doesn't shoot: every so often it emits a pulse around itself. Enemies with an aura, like the Guardian and the Healer, that the pulse reaches stop emitting it for a few seconds, and everything reached takes a very weak hit. It only switches off auras: it doesn't touch the Shaman, the Thief or the Rammer, and the Mirror stays outside the pulse. A suppressed enemy shows its ground ring broken and an icon of three arcs that switch off one by one. Those that had already received the aura lose it right away, and if another pulse arrives it doesn't add up: the longest time counts. How long each suppression lasts is in the tower's entry.

Flyers ignore the path: they go in a straight line from their entrance to the exit. Towers that can't hit flyers (see "Hits flyers" on each tower) don't even target them. You always need some tower that reaches the air.
Enemies wearing a golden crown are dangerous: if they reach the exit they take a lot of lives at once. It's worth saving your best towers for them.

The Boss resists slowing: Frost has half the effect on it. The Troll heals itself over time, but fire stops its healing. The Spider releases hatchlings when it dies, and the hatchlings count as enemies of the wave. Every enemy has its entry with all its data.
Every enemy you kill adds points according to the gold it gives. If you win, every life you have left adds more. You see the points at the top, next to the gold.
When you win a level you get 1 to 3 stars depending on how many lives you have left: the more, the better. The stars of all levels add up on the level selection screen.

Every level has its top 5, with three letters. Whoever wins all the levels enters the Hall of Fame, which adds up the best score of each level. Community maps have their own top 5 and don't count for the Hall.
On a phone you play by touching the screen: the buttons below choose the tower and the tower's panel has Upgrade and Sell.
